top3.headline: OpenAI reverses its Codex cut and doubles Pro usage limits
top3.whyItMatters: Vendor plan terms can flip within a day, so avoid locking agent budgets to one seat type.

top3.headline: Mistral releases open weights for a trillion-parameter coding model
top3.whyItMatters: A European open model near the coding frontier gives you a credible self-hosted fallback.

top3.headline: Anthropic expands free Claude credits to 20 science institutions
top3.whyItMatters: Anthropic says agents turn months of lab data analysis into hours, a pace worth testing.

items.title: Claude on iPad now opens its work beside the chat
items.takeaway: On iPad and iPhone Duo, what Claude makes opens next to the conversation and can go full screen.
items.soWhat: Putting output beside the chat lets people review AI work without losing the thread.

items.title: LangChain's hosted agents can now use a browser
items.takeaway: Managed Deep Agents 0.10, in public beta, adds browser use and async subagents for long background tasks.
items.soWhat: Agents can now work on sites with no API, with users signing in when needed.

items.title: OpenAI doubles Pro limits and drops the planned Codex cut
items.takeaway: Per @thsottiaux, limits double for Pro and Business Premium from Oct 29; Pro 200 Codex usage stays the same.
items.soWhat: Teams coding on Pro seats keep their allowance, so revisit plan changes prompted by the reported cut.

related.name: OpenAIDevs: API credits for Pro and Business

items.title: Anthropic hands free Claude credits to 20 science funders and institutes
items.takeaway: Partners include NSF, Sloan and the Crick Institute; a new draft standard lets agents run lab instruments.
items.soWhat: Science funders are now routing AI access through grants, not only individual lab budgets.

items.title: Mistral opens the weights of its trillion-parameter Large 4
items.takeaway: After more training, Mistral says it scores 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and ties GLM-5.3 on coding agents.
items.soWhat: Teams that need self-hosted or European models now have a frontier-class option for agentic coding.

items.title: Cursor agents rebuilt Slack as a video by watching the app
items.takeaway: @mattyp's 10-minute walkthrough covers computer use, inner and outer loops, skills and feedback loops.
items.soWhat: A worked example of agents learning from a live app, useful when designing agent workflows.

items.title: Amp: coding agents need a Mac only about 35% of the time
items.takeaway: @sqs says the finding shaped Amp's macOS Satellites, making Mac dev work faster and cheaper.
items.soWhat: Run most agent work on cheaper Linux machines and use Macs only for steps that need them.

voices.quote: won't be reducing usage limits for Pro 200, so your Work and Codex usage will stay the same
a lot of the challenges in harness engineering are now best solved by closer integration of harness and infra
Even for macOS-heavy dev, your agent only needs a Mac for ~35% of the time.
